title: The two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination: existence, uniqueness, and probabilistic interpretation
abstract: This entry formalizes the two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination, with finitely many alleles at each locus and parent-independent mutation. For positive mutation rates and nonnegative recombination rate, a solution exists and is unique, over any linearly ordered field. For real parameters, the solution at a sample typed at both loci equals the probability that the typed ancestral recombination graph, in which a mutation removes the ancestry of a lineage at that locus and assigns a type to the sample members it carries, ends with exactly the types of the sample. The solution sums to 1 over all typings of a sample of given size, tends to the product of the one-locus sampling probabilities as the recombination rate tends to infinity, and at recombination rate 0 gives a solution of a one-locus recursion on pairs of alleles. With mutation rates 0, the expected total branch length of the genealogy at locus A of a sample of size n is 2 times the sum of 1/(i + 1) for i < n − 1. The transition matrix of the typed ancestral chain is shown to be nonnegative with unit row sums.
